newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia PM pins hopes on new team to end pay delays.
newsitem.headline: Russia PM pins hopes on new team to end pay delays.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, opening the first session of his reshuffled cabinet on Thursday, said he hoped new first deputy Anatoly Chubais would help solve the problem of wage arrears.
"I hope that Anatoly Chubais' knowledge and experience will help us make colossal progress (in this field)," Interfax news agency quoted Chernomyrdin as saying.

Millions of Russians wait months to receive their wages and pensions. The government blames tax dodgers for the delays. Trade unions, backed by the communist opposition, will stage a national day of protests on March 27 against the arrears.

The reshuffle, which has still not been completed, has put liberal reformers like Chubais and regional governor Boris Nemtsev in broad control of economic policy in a bid to jump-start Russia's stalled reform programme.
Chubais, who is loathed by the communists for his pro-market views and his role in President Boris Yeltsin's re-election last July, is also finance minister in the new cabinet.
Later on Thursday Chubais will fly to Kemerovo, heart of the Kuzbass coal-mining region, for talks with angry miners.
Chernomyrdin said the timely payment of wages and pensions and other social issues would be the top priority of his new cabinet.
Chernomyrdin told the cabinet meeting that more personnel changes would be announced after Yeltsin returns to Moscow on Saturday from a summit meeting in Helsinki with U.S. President Bill Clinton.
Yeltsin was due to leave for the Finnish capital on Thursday at 1400 (1100 GMT), a presidential spokeswoman said.
